hints: Focus on the word prophase. Has DNA replication (S phase) already happened, so is each of the 46 chromosomes made of one or two chromatids?
Remember what a telomere is. It caps the end of a DNA molecule, so how many ends (and telomeres) does one single chromatid have?
walkthrough:
**Picture the cell in prophase**

Think of a human body cell about to divide by mitosis. It has 46 chromosomes, but DNA has already been copied in S phase. So in prophase each chromosome is X-shaped, made of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.

**Count the chromatids first**

This is the trick most students miss. Do not count chromosomes, count chromatids:
$$46 \text{ chromosomes} \times 2 \text{ chromatids per chromosome} = 92 \text{ chromatids}$$

**Count telomeres per chromatid**

A telomere is the protective cap at the end of a DNA molecule. Each chromatid contains one DNA molecule with two ends, so it has two telomeres, one at each end:
$$92 \text{ chromatids} \times 2 \text{ telomeres per chromatid} = 184 \text{ telomeres}$$ That gives option D.

options.A: Too low. It counts only 46 and forgets both that chromosomes are duplicated in prophase and that each chromatid has two ends.
options.B: Counts two ends per chromosome but forgets duplication. In prophase there are not 46 single chromatids, there are 92 chromatids.
options.C: Correctly counts 92 chromatids but then counts only one telomere per chromatid. Every chromatid has two ends, so two telomeres.
options.D: Correct. 46 duplicated chromosomes give 92 chromatids, and 92 chromatids times 2 ends each gives 184 telomeres.
